directorStatement.audienceFeeling: Jenny finds the magic helped her paper, and she feels a bit braver. Jenny says the word right, makes her own little joke, and the magic friends are secretly happy.
directorStatement.emotionalChange: Keep the magic secret and quiet; Jenny should not become suddenly fearless, only a little more able. End on modest triumph rather than applause: the final feeling is private confidence, shared kindness and a tiny hidden wink from The Fold.
directorStatement.theLaugh: Jenny wants to understand what has happened to her worksheet and card. Jenny wants to try the line again without being swallowed by the old embarrassment. She needs to carry the truth into the day physically, not just hear it once. She needs to discover that courage can include nervousness and even a remembered mistake.
directorStatement.visualSurprise: Morning brings Jenny back to the shoebox, where the worksheet is repaired with golden tape and the card waits beside it. She reads the message with confusion before a small smile arrives. Most importantly, she pockets the card and holds the worksheet without folding it smaller, showing the internal -> Jenny standing with the worksheet, ready for school.
directorStatement.carryForward: Jenny’s choice in class leaves the mistake included, not hidden, and the day can continue with a lighter private confidence.

northStar.surfaceStory: Jenny comes back to the shoebox morning after the mistake has been repaired. She sees the worksheet, reads the gold-taped fix, pockets the card, then later in class chooses to read the line again and adds her own joke to the old mistake.
northStar.universalTruth: Getting something wrong does not make you small; staying with it can make you braver.
northStar.childClearWant: Jenny wants to read the word correctly and not feel embarrassed again.
northStar.emotionalNeed: She needs to feel she can return to the mistake without shrinking away from it.
northStar.falseBeliefUnderPressure: If I get it wrong, I should hide or make myself smaller.
northStar.relationshipEngine: The teacher’s calm permission and the class’s kind laughter give Jenny room to stay in the moment; Nib’s distant joke helps her keep enough lightness to try again.
northStar.ordinaryLifeTruth: A small shame can make a child fold themselves down; being met gently lets them unfold.
northStar.sceneTurn: Jenny moves from reading the repaired message as if it were a warning to treating it as proof she can try again, then publicly owns the joke instead of hiding it.
audienceJourney: recognise the worry of going back to something you failed at
feel the quiet relief of a repaired mistake
enjoy the nervous courage of trying again
feel the laugh land safely when Jenny joins in
leave with the warm sense that a mistake can become part of the story, not the end of it
northStar.finalAfterFeeling: Quietly triumphant, lighter, and safe enough to be funny about it.
northStar.dialogueSubtractionOpportunity: The card and Jenny’s choice to pocket it can carry the meaning of the line; the smile and the way she holds the worksheet can reduce any need to spell out that she has learned something.
northStar.environmentPressure: The shoebox, worksheet, and gold tape all press the same idea: the mistake is still present, but now it must be handled rather than hidden. The classroom adds social pressure by making Jenny face the word again.

inputs.title: The Box That Felt Small
inputs.logline: After Jenny hides the shame of misreading a word, Patch leads the Box Monsters into a shoebox classroom where a giant mistake must become something she can try again with, not something that makes her small.

orderedEvents.text: Jenny stands at the front of the classroom holding her worksheet.
The word BRIDGE is written on the board.
Jenny looks at the word. Her fingers tighten around the paper.
One child lets out a tiny laugh. Another child laughs because the first one did.
Jenny looks at the word again. It feels much bigger now.
Final Frame: Jenny frozen, embarrassed, holding the worksheet close.

beats.storyBeat: Jenny stands in the exposed classroom space and tries to read the line. The ordinary word on the board becomes dangerous through silence, hesitation and the accidental wrong word. The tiny laugh is not cruelly staged, but it is enough to make Jenny’s body close around the worksheet and make her corrected answer come out small.
beats.want: Jenny wants to read the sentence correctly and get safely through her turn.
beats.need: She needs to know that a visible mistake does not reduce her worth.
beats.kidRead: It feels awful when you say something wrong and everyone hears it.
beats.adultRead: A small public stumble can become disproportionately huge inside a sensitive child, even when the adults respond gently.
beats.emotionalIntent: Let the audience feel the blush before the magic begins: embarrassment as a physical freeze, not a lesson.

beats.storyBeat: In her bedroom, Jenny brings the folded worksheet to her decorated shoebox, a safe place for treasured things. She tries to make the feeling disappear by placing it inside and closing the lid, not noticing that the box has received more than paper: it has received the feeling she cannot carry alone.

beats.need: She needs the hidden feeling to be met, not buried.
beats.kidRead: Jenny hides the paper because looking at it hurts.
beats.adultRead: The shoebox becomes a child’s private emotional container: a tender coping strategy that also signals isolation.
beats.emotionalIntent: Make the action intimate and gentle, with the box feeling like a confidant even before the magic answers.
